note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM F, team 1904381: a three-market macroeconomic model built to answer what happens when
a digital currency is introduced. Money demand is derived at the individual level from a
Cobb-Douglas utility over two currencies, the LM/IS/FE triple is assembled from it, two
exchange-rate institutions are run through a policy-assignment analysis, and R anova output is
offered as the sensitivity and robustness check. Twenty-eight pages, twenty-one of which carry
art, forty measured regions.

**All forty are accounted**: 2 native tables, 37 figure rows (of which 17 are panels of the
eleven numbered figures, 9 are uncaptioned body plates, 11 are uncaptioned appendix plates) and
1 refusal. The refusal is p22, a full-page raster of the team's letter to the judges.

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 2.2 "Notation of Parameters" takes **Table 1**, the 31-row notation grid, above the text.
- 3.1 "Digital Currency System" takes the **chevron timeline**, uncaptioned, called only "the
  figure above".
- 3.2.2 takes **Figure 1**; 3.2.3 takes **Figures 2 and 3** — five of them are the same
  four-quadrant template, and 3.3/3.4 take **Figures 4 and 5**, which are Word tables.
- 4.2.1 takes **Table 2** and the p12 roadmap plate; 4.2.2 takes **Figure 6** (the one real
  flowchart); 4.2.3 takes **Figures 7 and 8** (two more Word tables); 4.2.4 takes the **Swan
  pair**; 4.3.2 takes the **floating-rate matrix** and the **three p17 plates**.
- 4.5.1 takes the **Sweden 3-D plot**; 4.5.1/4.5.2 take **Figure 9**; 5.1 takes **Figure 10**;
  5.2 takes **Figure 11**.
- The appendix takes **eleven 3-D stem plots**, grouped two-three-two-three-one by country.

## When it goes 3-D

**Only where a third variable has to be shown, and only in the appendix plus one body plate.**
Twelve of the thirty-seven figure rows are 3-D, and eleven of those twelve are the appendix;
the body's one 3-D plate is the Sweden domestic-product model on p18. Every 3-D object is an R
`persp`-style box with vertical stems standing on a base plane, ticked on all three axes, with
the depth variable named only in the rotated right-margin title (`M/P` on money-market plates,
`G/TAN` on domestic-product plates, a bare `I` on foreign-exchange plates). The paper never
fakes depth: the fifty-eight flat 2-D objects (schedules, matrices, grids, flowcharts) carry no
shading, no perspective and no colourbar anywhere.

## What the figures do

| group | count | what it actually is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Figures 1-3 | 6 panels | one four-quadrant LM template, reused five times, with an equation strip pasted on top |
| Figures 4, 5, 7, 8, 10 | 6 panels | **rasterised Word tables and R console output captioned as figures** |
| Figure 6 | 1 | the only real mechanism flowchart: money supply -> interest rate -> two accounts |
| Figures 9, 11 | 4 panels | IS/LM/FE line charts, three straight schedules, legend drifting between inside and outside |
| Swan pair, p12, p15b, p16, p17a-c | 8 | policy-assignment matrices, a roadmap, and a fiscal-transmission schematic |
| appendix | 11 | 3-D stem plots, one title per plate |

## Table shapes worth reusing

The paper prints only two native grids, and their dress is chosen by content, not by convention:

| table | shape | trick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table 1 notation | 31x2, open sides | thin rule between every row, one heavier rule under the header, ONE vertical divider, no left or right frame |
| Table 2 balance sheet | 5x2, fully boxed | a frame and a full internal rule set appear only when the grid has to be read as two facing columns |

Everything else that looks tabular is a picture: four case-wheels (`Above`/`Below` x
`Curve slope size`/`Curve panning`), two anova consoles, a colour-coded 2x2 matrix, a
capital-flow sensitivity grid, and a four-column summary with a merged conclusion row. **The
moment a table needs a merged stub, a filled header band or a colour cell, the authors stopped
typesetting and pasted a screenshot** — the six raster grids carry every merge in the file, and
the two typeset grids carry none.

## Caption template

`Figure N:` or `Table N:` — a COLON on all thirteen numbered captions, and no period anywhere.
Then a bare noun phrase: `The slope`, `LM Curve shifts`, `The analysis of the IS model`,
`Mechanism`, `linear regression anova result`, `Central bank's assets and liabilities`. Four to
nine words, no unit, no variable, no condition, no conclusion, nominal in voice. The caption
prints BELOW its exhibit on eleven of thirteen (Table 1 is the exception, above), and the same
caption word is reused without embarrassment: `Figure 6: Mechanism`, `Figure 7: Mechanism`,
`Figure 8: Mechanism` over a flowchart and two Word tables.

## Context connectives

- The dominant pointer is **"<Number> <verb>"** inside a full sentence: `Figure 1 explains the
  economic meaning of points that are not on the curve.`, `Figure 2 demonstrates that the slope
  of the LM curve is determined by ...`, `Figure 3 explains why LM curve will shift to the right`,
  `According to the Figure 11, Thailand should pursue a tight fiscal policy`. Six exhibits are
  named this way, and the number is always capital-F, always inside a sentence, never in a
  parenthetical.
- The second form is **"The mechanism works as follows."** — five words, deictic, naming
  nothing — used for Figures 6 and 7, the two objects of completely different genus.
- The third is **"the figure above"**, used twice: for the chevron timeline, which has no
  caption at all, and for the p18 3-D plate, whose sentence opens `From the figure above and
  Firgue9` — a misspelling of the very figure number two pages later.
- The read-backs are verdicts: `From the linear regression result above, we can conclude that
  each variables of the model is indispensable`, and for the results pair, a named policy
  recommendation per country.

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **The layout pass files every panel of Figures 1-3 against a list heading.** All six panels
  come back as `3 Balance: ...` because the numbered list items of 3.2.3 are parsed as headings;
  the real owners are 3.2.2 and 3.2.3.
- **The whole appendix is filed under `References`**, because `Appendix A Real Data Result`
  first prints on p26 while nine of the eleven plates sit on p24-p25.
- **Figure 9's panel letters begin at (c).** The p19 pair prints `(c) result for Sweden` and
  `(d) result for Israel`; there is no (a) and no (b) anywhere in the file. Panel letters
  restart at (a) for Figure 10 on the same page, so the letters are per-figure and the first
  two of Figure 9 were simply never printed.
- **The text layer hyphenates within sentences** (`international mone- tary system`), so every
  quoted lead and trail in this record is a literal slice of the layer, hyphen and all.
- **p22 has no text layer at all** — 29 characters, all running head — because the page is a
  scanned letter.
- **The pointer on p17 names the wrong genus**: `the following table can be summarized` stands
  over a flowchart, a grid and a second grid, and only two of the three are tables.
- **Table 1's foot rule falls outside its measured region**, so the closing rule under the last
  row (`γ, n, σ, φ`) is not inside the bbox even though the table is.

## Declared deficits

**Figure 9 is short two panels.** Its caption reads "three model together result for Sweden and

rules: Exhibit type is chosen by what has to be said, not by the caption word: the paper needs a flowchart for a mechanism (one), a matrix for a policy assignment (five), a line chart for an equilibrium result (four), a 3-D stem plot for a third variable (twelve) and a grid for a notation list (two). [place.section_kind]

The 3-D form is reserved for the case where a third variable must be shown, and it is confined to the appendix almost entirely: eleven of the twelve 3-D rows are appendix plates and the twelfth is the one country-model plot in the body. [geometry.three_d]

Depth is never faked on the flat objects: no colourbar, no surface mesh, no isometric projection and no shading appears on any of the fifty-eight 2-D plates, matrices and schematics in the file. [geometry.colorbar]
A numbered caption is a COLON form on all thirteen rows - 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:' - never a period, and the appendix plates carry no number and no caption at all. [caption.numbering]

Captions are bare noun phrases of four to nine words - 'The slope', 'Mechanism', 'linear regression anova result' - and not one states a unit, names a variable, gives a condition or draws a conclusion. [caption.words]

The caption prints BELOW the exhibit on eleven of thirteen numbered rows; only Table 1, the notation grid, puts its caption above, which is what lets it be read as the head of the symbol list. [caption.position]
The same caption word is reused across objects of entirely different genus: 'Mechanism' names a flowchart (Figure 6) and then two Word tables (Figures 7 and 8) without change. [caption.verbatim]

The dominant pointer names the number inside a full sentence - 'Figure 2 demonstrates that the slope of the LM curve is determined by ...' - on six rows, always capital-F and never in a parenthetical. [mention.lead_pattern]

The weakest pointer in the file is five words long and names nothing - 'The mechanism works as follows.' - and it is the only pointer used for two of the five numbered objects it introduces. [mention.lead_sentence]

The read-back is a verdict rather than a reading: after the anova pair the prose concludes the model is 'insensitive to the outliers', and after the robustness pair it prescribes a policy per country, but no row ever quotes a cell or a coefficient. [mention.trail_sentence]
Rows whose exhibit is named only by its own caption record count 0 - Figures 4, 5, 8 and the eleven appendix plates are never referred to by number anywhere in the running text. [mention.count]

Two grids are typeset and thirty-four are not: the typeset pair uses thin horizontal rules with at most one vertical divider, and every grid that can be read as two facing columns gets a full frame instead. [table.rule_style]
Column separators appear only when the grid is a balance sheet: Table 2 draws one vertical rule between assets and liabilities, and no other typeset grid draws any. [table.cols]
Grid breadth follows content, not the page: the notation list is set to the full text measure because its descriptions run long, and the balance sheet stops at half. [table.width]

No typeset grid merges a cell and no typeset grid shades a row; every merge in the file (six of them) and every fill (two of them) belongs to a grid that was pasted as a screenshot instead. [table.merged_cells]

Merged stubs are the signal for switching to a picture: the 'Mechanism' and 'Policy Effect' stubs, the merged title band and the merged conclusion row all live inside raster grids, never inside the two typeset ones. [table.header_rows]

The legend drifts: the two panels of Figure 9 put the same key inside the axes on the left and outside the axes on the right, and the appendix plates drop the key entirely and leave a red stem group unkeyed. [geometry.legend]

tables.note: the whole notation of the model in one 31-row grid: a bold 'Parameters' header over 'Descriptions', thin horizontals between every row, a heavier rule under the header, and exactly one vertical rule between the two columns — no outer box on the left or right, so the grid is a ruled list rather than a framed table. Two-line wrapping in ten rows (m̄, α,β, L1(Y), L2(i), M̄s, M̄s1, M̄s2, Pf, e). The notation itself is damaged: M̄s and M̄s2 are BOTH glossed 'in the form of digital currency', which leaves M̄s1 as the only traditional-money row; L2(i) is glossed 'a function with regards to interest rate'; P is 'Price level measured by inflation rate'.

tables.note: a two-column balance sheet, fully boxed — outer frame, one vertical rule between the columns, a horizontal rule on every row — which makes it the only framed grid in the file, Table 1 being open on both sides. Five asset rows against three liability rows, so the right column prints blank beside 'International reserve assets' and 'Foreign exchange assets'. Two cells carry a printed upward arrow glyph (after 'Base currency' and after 'International reserve assets') as an in-cell mark, not as column data; they are typeset characters inside the cell text, so a text-layer reader sees 'Base currency ⇑' as one string.
